items.answer: It includes a share of fixed production overheads in each unit, whereas marginal costing includes only variable production costs.

items.stem: Explain why absorption costing is required for published financial statements.
items.answer: IAS 2 requires inventory cost to include all costs of bringing it to its present condition, including production overheads, matching costs to revenue.

items.markingKey: Error explained: contribution per limiting factor is required [1]; working: match the purpose to the method [1]; correct method: marginal costing [1] [3]

items.stem: Aurora Printing needs to rank products when labour hours are scarce. State which costing method is more appropriate in each case and explain why.
items.answer: marginal costing – contribution per limiting factor is required.
items.markingKey: marginal costing [1]; contribution per limiting factor is required [1] [2]

items.stem: Monsoon Garments needs to rank products when labour hours are scarce and also finds that managers increase production at the year end to boost reported profit. (a) State which costing method is more appropriate in each case and explain why. (b) Recommend which costing method Monsoon Garments should use for setting prices of a new product.
items.answer: (a) marginal costing – contribution per limiting factor is required; marginal costing – profit then depends on sales, not on inventory build-up. (b) Absorption cost-plus ensures all costs are covered in the long run; marginal pricing may be used for special orders; the choice depends on the market.
